traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.38, 0.3, 0.24], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.crown_form.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 363): 'short stout more or less contorted branches spreading almost at right angles and forming a narrow usually flat-topped head'.

traits.limb_course.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 363): 'short stout more or less contorted branches spreading almost at right angles'.

traits.limb_angle.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 363): 'short stout more or less contorted branches spreading almost at right angles and forming a narrow usually flat-topped head'.

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Sassafras albidum (read 2026-10-18): "In fall, they turn to shades of yellow, tinged with red". Colour ours.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's sassafras review (Sullivan 1993, read 2026-10-16): up to 98 feet (30 m) on the best sites; in the north often shrubby, to 40 feet (12 m). FNA vol. 3 gives trees to 35 m.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade 10-16 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade 5-10 cm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade ovate to elliptic, unlobed or 2-3-lobed.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): unlobed or 2-3-lobed, rarely more; Simpson p. 197 shows unlobed, mitten-shaped and three-lobed leaves on one shoot.

traits.leaf_lobes.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): 2-3 lobes where lobed.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's sassafras review (Sullivan 1993, read 2026-10-16): "a native, deciduous, aromatic tree or large shrub".

traits.bark_texture.note: FEIS's sassafras review (Sullivan 1993, read 2026-10-16): bark of older stems deeply furrowed, or broken into broad flat ridges.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): staminate and pistillate flowers described apart.

traits.inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it, FNA saying only that the clusters reach 5 cm.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): inflorescences to 5 cm; the shortest is the model estimate's (species-facts-2026-10-15).

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): tepals greenish yellow. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): a drupe about 1 cm on a reddish, club-shaped, rather fleshy stalk.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): drupe about 1 cm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Sassafras albidum (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowering April-May.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

generator.params.note: Red alder's crown values, changed by hand: one trunk with short, stout limbs held out wide (FEIS: a flattened, oblong crown), path_half fitted so it reaches its height. Not fitted to measurements. spur_leaf is the leaf card the angiosperm rule gives leaf_size, 1.5 times the flora's mean blade, so short-shoot leaves are drawn the same size. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: 13 m at 30 years in the open, within FEIS's heights (to 30 m on the best sites, 12 m in the north). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after FEIS and FNA vol. 3: red-brown, deeply furrowed bark; leaves drawn three-lobed, the most distinctive of the unlobed, mitten and three-lobed leaves one tree bears, with broad, rounded lobes cut to half the radius, as iNaturalist photographs show them (observations 264729413, 112901363).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2591964), as no source read gives it.

traits.rosette.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2591964), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_margin.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2591964), as no source read gives it.

traits.fruit_cup_colour.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2, sassafras (read 2026-10-17): a dark blue drupe on a thickened red pedicel; WPSM: on thick red pedicels; FNA (via a SEINet mirror) 'pedicel reddish, club-shaped, fleshy', expanded with the perianth into a cup-like base. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.fruits_per_inflorescence.note: Not counted in a flora read (2026-10-17): Silvics calls the racemes loose and few-flowered and WPSM has the drupes in clusters on thick red pedicels; one to four set, as photographs show, is our estimate.
